instructions:
Drive a real or simulated iOS/Android device.

Start with mobile_list_available_devices and pass the chosen device id to every
later call - there is no implicit "current device". Use a remote device only
when local ones do not fit or when requested by the user. Remote devices cost
money and take time to allocate and release. Release when done using, so the
remote device cleans and returns to pool.

Read the screen with mobile_list_elements_on_screen, not screenshots: it returns
refs, coordinates and labels, and tapping by ref survives layout differences
between devices. Fall back to mobile_take_screenshot only for elements missing
from the hierarchy, or to judge visual appearance.

Each call is a device round-trip. Group known sequences (tap, type, tap) into
mobile_batch_commands instead of issuing them one at a time.

Prefer mobile_launch_app to open an app, and mobile_open_url to open a web page,
over navigating through the UI. mobile_open_url only accepts http:// and
https:// URLs unless the server was started with MOBILEMCP_ALLOW_UNSAFE_URLS=1,
so do not rely on it for app deep links.

tools.name: get_more_tools
tools.title: Get More Tools
tools.description: Only call this when none of the other tools can do what you need on a mobile device, or for mobile testing or mobile app development. Do not call it for tasks unrelated to mobile, or when another tool already covers the task. The context is sent to the mobile-mcp developers, so never include PII, secrets, credentials or other private information in it.

context.description: A description of your goal and what kind of tool would help accomplish it.

tools.name: mobile_list_available_devices
tools.title: List Devices
tools.description: List all available devices. This includes both physical mobile devices and mobile simulators and emulators. It returns both Android and iOS devices. These are local devices already connected to this machine, ready to use immediately at no cost - for devices from the shared remote cloud fleet, use mobile_list_remote_devices instead.

tools.name: mobile_login_to_cloud_provider
tools.title: Login to Cloud Provider
tools.description: Start authenticating this machine with the remote device cloud provider. This is required once before mobile_list_remote_devices or mobile_allocate_remote_device will work; if either of those fails with an authentication error, call this tool and then retry. This starts a browser-based device-code login and returns quickly with a URL and a one-time code - it does NOT wait for the login to complete. Show the URL and code to the user verbatim and ask them to open the URL and enter the code in their own browser. The login keeps running in the background after this tool returns; once the user confirms they've completed it, retry the remote devices tool that originally failed. Only call this after the user has asked for, or agreed to, remote/cloud devices - never call it speculatively, since it interrupts the user to act in their browser.

tools.name: mobile_list_remote_devices
tools.title: List Remote Devices
tools.description: List the catalog of device models (make, platform, OS version) available to reserve from the remote cloud device fleet. This is different from mobile_list_available_devices, which lists real devices and simulators/emulators already connected to this local machine and ready to use immediately at no cost. Remote devices live in a shared cloud fleet: they are not usable until reserved with mobile_allocate_remote_device, and reserving one may be a limited/billed resource. Requires mobile_login_to_cloud_provider to have been called first; if this fails with an authentication error, call that tool then retry.

tools.name: mobile_allocate_remote_device
tools.title: Allocate Remote Device
tools.description: Reserve a physical device from the remote cloud fleet for exclusive use, returning a device identifier usable with the other mobile_* tools. Unlike local devices, a remote device is a shared and billed resource borrowed for the session - never call this silently. If no local device is available, offer a remote device to the user and call this only after they agree. Requires mobile_login_to_cloud_provider to have been called first; if this fails with an authentication error, call that tool then retry. Use mobile_list_remote_devices first to see which names and versions actually exist in the fleet before filtering by them. Release the device with mobile_release_remote_device once the whole task is finished - releasing wipes the device's state, so do not release and reallocate between steps of the same task just to be tidy.

platform.description: The platform to allocate a device for

name.description: Filter by device name/model. Supports a trailing * for prefix match (e.g. "iPhone*"), or an exact name (e.g. "iPhone 16").

version.description: Filter by OS version. Supports comparison prefixes >=, >, <=, < (e.g. ">=18"), or an exact version (e.g. "18.6.2"). Multiple values are ANDed together.

type.description: Device type filter. Currently only "real" (physical devices) is supported by the fleet.

wait.description: If true, block until the device has finished allocating and is ready to use, up to timeoutSeconds. If false/omitted, this returns as soon as the reservation is made, but the device may not be immediately ready.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for allocation when wait is true. Defaults to 900 (15 minutes). Only relevant when wait is true.

tools.name: mobile_release_remote_device
tools.title: Release Remote Device
tools.description: Release a device previously reserved with mobile_allocate_remote_device back to the remote cloud fleet so it becomes available to others. Releasing is destructive to the device's state: apps installed, files pushed, and any other changes made during this session are lost, and a later mobile_allocate_remote_device call may take time and could return a different physical unit. Only release once the whole task is finished - if there is more work to do on the same device shortly, keep holding it rather than releasing and reallocating.

device.description: The device identifier to release back to the remote fleet

tools.name: mobile_list_apps
tools.title: List Apps
tools.description: List all the installed apps on the device

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

tools.name: mobile_get_foreground_app
tools.title: Get Foreground App
tools.description: Get the app currently in the foreground on the device, including the focused activity class on Android or view controller class on iOS when available. Use this to verify which app or screen you are on before interacting with it.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

tools.name: mobile_launch_app
tools.title: Launch App
tools.description: Launch an app on mobile device. Use this to open a specific app. You can find the package name of the app by calling mobile_list_apps.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

packageName.description: The package name of the app to launch

locale.description: Comma-separated BCP 47 locale tags to launch the app with (e.g., fr-FR,en-GB)

tools.name: mobile_terminate_app
tools.title: Terminate App
tools.description: Stop and terminate an app on mobile device

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

packageName.description: The package name of the app to terminate

tools.name: mobile_clear_app_data
tools.title: Clear App Data
tools.description: Clear an app's data, such as its cache, documents, preferences and databases, and stop the app, so the next launch starts as if freshly installed. The app stays installed. Supported on Android devices and emulators and on iOS simulators, not on real iOS devices.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

packageName.description: The package name (Android) or bundle id (iOS) of the app to clear

tools.name: mobile_install_app
tools.title: Install App
tools.description: Install an app on mobile device

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

path.description: The path to the app file to install. For iOS simulators, provide a .zip file or a .app directory. For Android provide an .apk file. For iOS real devices provide an .ipa file

tools.name: mobile_uninstall_app
tools.title: Uninstall App
tools.description: Uninstall an app from mobile device

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

packageName.description: The package name of the app to uninstall

tools.name: mobile_get_screen_size
tools.title: Get Screen Size
tools.description: Get the screen size of the mobile device in pixels

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

tools.name: mobile_click_on_screen_at_coordinates
tools.title: Click Screen
tools.description: Click on the screen, either at x,y coordinates or on an element by its ref (e.g. "@e5") from the latest mobile_list_elements_on_screen result. Prefer ref when the element is listed.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

x.description: The x coordinate to click on the screen, in pixels. Required unless ref is given

y.description: The y coordinate to click on the screen, in pixels. Required unless ref is given

ref.description: Element ref from mobile_list_elements_on_screen, e.g. "@e5". Takes precedence over x,y

tools.name: mobile_double_tap_on_screen
tools.title: Double Tap Screen
tools.description: Double-tap on the screen, either at x,y coordinates or on an element by its ref (e.g. "@e5") from the latest mobile_list_elements_on_screen result. Prefer ref when the element is listed.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

x.description: The x coordinate to double-tap, in pixels. Required unless ref is given

y.description: The y coordinate to double-tap, in pixels. Required unless ref is given

ref.description: Element ref from mobile_list_elements_on_screen, e.g. "@e5". Takes precedence over x,y

tools.name: mobile_long_press_on_screen_at_coordinates
tools.title: Long Press Screen
tools.description: Long press on the screen, either at x,y coordinates or on an element by its ref (e.g. "@e5") from the latest mobile_list_elements_on_screen result. Prefer ref when the element is listed.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

x.description: The x coordinate to long press on the screen, in pixels. Required unless ref is given

y.description: The y coordinate to long press on the screen, in pixels. Required unless ref is given

ref.description: Element ref from mobile_list_elements_on_screen, e.g. "@e5". Takes precedence over x,y

duration.description: Duration of the long press in milliseconds. Defaults to 500ms.

tools.name: mobile_list_elements_on_screen
tools.title: List Screen Elements
tools.description: List elements on screen with their ref, coordinates, and display text or accessibility label. Use the ref with mobile_click_on_screen_at_coordinates, mobile_double_tap_on_screen or mobile_long_press_on_screen_at_coordinates. Refs and coordinates stay valid as long as the screen does not change; re-list only after navigation or a layout change.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

format.description: Output format. "text" (default) is one compact line per element, "json" is a json array, "raw" is the unfiltered platform-specific hierarchy as JSON (mobilecli only). Raw nodes may be offscreen and do not have element refs

tools.name: mobile_press_button
tools.title: Press Button
tools.description: Press a button on device

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

button.description:
The button to press, in upper case. Supported buttons:
Android: HOME, BACK, VOLUME_UP, VOLUME_DOWN, ENTER, BACKSPACE, APP_SWITCH, POWER, DPAD_CENTER, DPAD_UP, DPAD_DOWN, DPAD_LEFT, DPAD_RIGHT
iOS: HOME, VOLUME_UP, VOLUME_DOWN, ENTER, LOCK
BACKSPACE deletes the character before the cursor, APP_SWITCH opens the recent apps, POWER turns the screen on or off, LOCK locks the screen, and the DPAD buttons move focus on Android TV.

tools.name: mobile_open_url
tools.title: Open URL
tools.description: Open an http:// or https:// URL in the browser on device. Other URL schemes, such as app deep links, are rejected unless the server was started with MOBILEMCP_ALLOW_UNSAFE_URLS=1.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

url.description: The URL to open, starting with http:// or https://

tools.name: mobile_swipe_on_screen
tools.title: Swipe Screen
tools.description: Swipe on the screen

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

x.description: The x coordinate to start the swipe from, in pixels. Give both x and y, or neither to start from the center of screen

y.description: The y coordinate to start the swipe from, in pixels. Give both x and y, or neither to start from the center of screen

distance.description: The distance to swipe in pixels. Defaults to 400 pixels for iOS or 30% of screen dimension for Android

tools.name: mobile_type_keys
tools.title: Type Text
tools.description: Type text into the focused element

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

submit.description: Whether to submit the text. If true, the text will be submitted as if the user pressed the enter key. Defaults to false

tools.name: mobile_save_screenshot
tools.title: Save Screenshot
tools.description: Save a screenshot of the mobile device to a file

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

saveTo.description: The path to save the screenshot to. Filename must end with .png, .jpg, or .jpeg

maxSize.description: Maximum width/height in pixels, keeping aspect ratio. Omit for full size.

scale.description: Scale factor (0.0-1.0). Ignored if maxSize is provided.

tools.name: mobile_take_screenshot
tools.title: Take Screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the mobile device. Use this to understand what's on screen, if you need to press an element that is available through view hierarchy then you must list elements on screen instead. The screenshot is usually smaller than the screen, so when the device reports its screen size the result also states how to convert positions in the screenshot into screen coordinates before tapping. Do not cache this result.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

maxSize.description: Maximum width/height in pixels, keeping aspect ratio. Defaults to 1024.

scale.description: Scale factor (0.0-1.0). Ignored if maxSize is provided.

tools.name: mobile_set_orientation
tools.title: Set Orientation
tools.description: Change the screen orientation of the device

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

tools.name: mobile_fold_device
tools.title: Fold Device
tools.description: Fold or unfold a foldable device, such as iPhone Duo simulators and foldable Android emulators. Provide either posture or angle.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

posture.description: The desired hinge posture: folded (0 degrees), half-open (90 degrees) or open (180 degrees)

angle.description: The desired hinge angle in degrees, between 0 (folded) and 180 (open). iOS only, e.g. iPhone Duo. Use instead of posture.

tools.name: mobile_set_location
tools.title: Set Location
tools.description: Override the GPS location reported by the device, or clear the override to restore the real location. Omit latitude and longitude to clear.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

latitude.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, e.g. 37.7749. Omit together with longitude to clear the override.

longitude.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, e.g. -122.4194. Omit together with latitude to clear the override.

tools.name: mobile_clipboard
tools.title: Clipboard
tools.description: Read or replace the device clipboard. Pass text to set the clipboard, omit it to read the current clipboard.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

text.description: Text to place on the clipboard. Omit to read the clipboard instead.

tools.name: mobile_get_device_logs
tools.title: Get Device Logs
tools.description: Collect live device logs (logcat on Android, unified log on iOS) as one JSON object per line. Only logs emitted after the call starts are captured, so trigger the behavior you want to observe right before or during the call. Stops after `limit` entries or after 30 seconds of silence. Each line of a stack trace counts as one entry, so filter by process or tag to avoid filling the limit with noise. Start with a small limit (20-50) for a quick look. For large captures, pass `saveTo` to write logs to a file and only the entry count is returned.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

limit.description: Stop after this many log entries

filter.description: Filters, ANDed together. key=value includes, key!=value excludes. Keys: pid, process, tag, level, subsystem, category, message. Example: ["tag=ActivityManager", "level=Error", "process!=SpringBoard"]

saveTo.description: Path to write the logs to instead of returning them. Filename must end with .log, .txt, or .jsonl

tools.name: mobile_get_orientation
tools.title: Get Orientation
tools.description: Get the current screen orientation of the device

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

tools.name: mobile_start_screen_recording
tools.title: Start Screen Recording
tools.description: Start recording the screen of a mobile device. The recording runs in the background until stopped with mobile_stop_screen_recording. Returns the path where the recording will be saved.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

output.description: The file path to save the recording to. Filename must end with .mp4. If not provided, a temporary path will be used.

timeLimit.description: Maximum recording duration in seconds. The recording will stop automatically after this time.

tools.name: mobile_stop_screen_recording
tools.title: Stop Screen Recording
tools.description: Stop an active screen recording on a mobile device. Returns the file path, size, and approximate duration of the recording.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

tools.name: mobile_list_crashes
tools.title: List Crash Reports
tools.description: List crash reports available on the device

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

tools.name: mobile_get_crash
tools.title: Get Crash Report
tools.description: Get the full content of a crash report by its ID. Use mobile_list_crashes to find available crash IDs.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

id.description: The crash report ID to retrieve

tools.name: mobile_batch_commands
tools.title: Batch Commands
tools.description: Run multiple tools in sequence in a single call, e.g. click, type, click, type. Use this to fill forms or perform multi-step flows without round-trips. The device argument is applied to every step unless a step provides its own. Tools allowed as steps: get_more_tools, mobile_list_available_devices, mobile_login_to_cloud_provider, mobile_list_remote_devices, mobile_allocate_remote_device, mobile_release_remote_device, mobile_list_apps, mobile_get_foreground_app, mobile_launch_app, mobile_terminate_app, mobile_clear_app_data, mobile_install_app, mobile_uninstall_app, mobile_get_screen_size, mobile_click_on_screen_at_coordinates, mobile_double_tap_on_screen, mobile_long_press_on_screen_at_coordinates, mobile_list_elements_on_screen, mobile_press_button, mobile_open_url, mobile_swipe_on_screen, mobile_type_keys, mobile_save_screenshot, mobile_set_orientation, mobile_fold_device, mobile_set_location, mobile_clipboard, mobile_get_device_logs, mobile_get_orientation, mobile_start_screen_recording, mobile_stop_screen_recording, mobile_list_crashes, mobile_get_crash.

device.description: The device identifier to use. Use mobile_list_available_devices to find which devices are available to you.

name.description: Name of a tool allowed as a step, e.g. mobile_click_on_screen_at_coordinates

arguments.description: Arguments for the tool, same as calling it directly

stopOnError.description: Stop at the first failing step. Defaults to true

listElementsAtEnd.description: Run mobile_list_elements_on_screen after the last step and include its result. Defaults to false
